Use N–mm–MPa units and Euler–Bernoulli beam theory (small deflection, linear elastic).
Model a cantilever beam of length L = 1800 mm, fixed at x = 0 and free at x = L.
Material is structural steel with E = 200000 MPa and constant second moment of area I = 1200000 mm^4.
Apply a single downward point load P = 2000 N at the free end.
Do not apply any external couple at the free end; the free-end rotation is therefore nonzero.
Use the physically correct cantilever solution with linearly varying bending moment M(x) = −P(L−x), maximum at the fixed end and zero at the free end; do not use the constant-moment assumption.
Compute the free-end slope as θ = P·L² / (2·E·I).
Compute the free-end vertical deflection as δ = P·L³ / (3·E·I).
With the given values, report θ = 0.0135 rad (approximately 0.7738 degrees).
With the given values, report δ = 16.2 mm.
State that the free-end deflection is directed downward.
